about.text: The Armenian name (չորթան) for dried tan, the buttermilk left after butter is churned from matsun; dried into a hard, keeping food like the qurut of Central Asia.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Matsun churned to butter; the buttermilk is boiled and churned to a ricotta-like curd, shaped into balls and sun-dried for over a week
Crushed in water to make tan again, for soups such as tanapur and tarkhana

sources.text: Its names and facts, from these.
